description: A basic, run-of-the-mill type of "boom stick."
name: Shotgun
note:
<tjsWeapon>
<tjsWeaponType:shotgun>
<tjsGearType:weapon>
<tjsLevel:1>
<tjsWeaponDurability:auto>
<tjsTraitsMaxTacticalPoints:[25,112]>
<tjsGroup>
<tjsLeveledRates>
<tjsInfo:
(Shotgun) A basic,
run-of-the-mill "boom stick" of some
kind, pump-action shotguns are simplistic
firearms that characters of any class can
use.  While being considered a primary
weapon, and thusly taking up a single
primary weapon equipment slot, they are
something of a fallback weapon that one
can use if a preferred weapon specific to
one's character class is broken or
unavailable.  As such, they don't do as
much damage to opponents as better
weapons will, although they tend to be
low-cost and commonly found in weapon
stores.  Like all firearms, the damage
they do doesn't vary depending on ability
scores of the character wielding them.
Like all weapons, they will wear out and
break after being used a certain number
of times, and then need to be thrown out
and replaced.
>

description:
A quick-and-fast machine pistol that can fire many shots rapidly, in bursts as well as a classic "lead hose" type of attack.  Can attack multiple targets at once.
Does plain physical damage.
name: SMG
note:
<tjsWeapon>
<tjsWeaponType:smg>
<tjsGearType:weapon>
<tjsLevel:1>
<tjsWeaponDurability:auto>
<tjsTpMod:auto>
<tjsTraitsMaxTacticalPoints:[100,132]>
<tjsGroup>
<tjsLeveledRates>
<tjsInfo:(SMG) A quick-and-fast machine pistol that can fire many shots rapidly, in bursts as well as a classic "lead hose" type of attack.  Can attack multiple targets at once.  SMGs can easily be held and
used with only one hand, allowing the individual wielding it to also equip a shield, or in some other way have their other hand free.  SMGs are not the most powerful firearms, but fare better in
combat than backup weapons, such as pistols.  They are good at shooting many enemies at once.  SMGs can be used by Rifleman and Ninja character classes.  Regular SMGs do plain physical damage,
although there are versions that are enchanted, which shoot bullets that do elemental wind or elemental earth damage.  Like many weapons, SMGS can only be used so many times before they break.>

<tjsInfo:(Assault Rifle) Assault rifles fire in single shots, bursts, and barrages, and do heavy damage to their targets.  They can attack multiple targets at once.  Equipping an assault rifle takes two hands
to do, and as such a character wielding an assault rifle cannot equip a shield of any sort.  Assault rifles are the most damaging weapons of all standard firearms a Rifleman can equip and use.  They

description:
(Longsword) A good strong longsword, designed to be used with one or two hands.  Good for basic hack-and-slash.
Does plain physical damage.

<tjsGroup>
<tjsLeveledRates>
<tjsInfo:
(Longsword) A good sharp, strong
longsword, designed to be used with one
or two hands.  Good for basic
hack-and-slash.  Single longswords like
these allow one to also equip a shield.
Most common longswords do plain physical
damage, although some are enchanted to do
a combination of physical and magical
elemental damage, with the element
typically being elemental fire, ice,
lightning, or acid.  Note that enchanted
longswords that do elemental acid damage
don't create lasting acid burns into
following turns in combat, but instead do
all of their damage right away, like most
other swords, and mundane weaponry.
Longswords can be equipped by Swordmaster
and Cleric class characters.
>
<tjsInfo2:
    Longswords don't typically require or
use any Magic Points from a character's
spirit to operate.  Basic attacks don't
cost any Tactical Points either, and do
damage based upon one's strength score
and the level of the sword.
\LB    Longswords are very fast compared
to other melee weapons, and do a decent
amount of damage by comparison.  They
increase a character's maximum Tactical
Points by a really good amount when
equipped.  They add more to Tactical
Points than dual longswords, and also
substantially increase the rate at which
Tactical Points are gained and recovered.
The only melee weapons that do these
things better would be two-handed swords,
although longswords allow for a shield to
be equipped while two-handed swords do
not.
\LB    Melee weapons and other types of
items have levels, and versions of an
item with a higher level are more
expensive when purchased from a merchant
but do more damage when wielded by a
character with the same starting strength
score.  Different level versions of a
weapon or other item have associated
materials that are in the name of the
item, such as "iron" or "glass" or
"marble" for example, which refer to
reagents used and consumed during the
artificing process to enchant and create
such items, which are typically magical.
As an example, a "glass sword" doesn't
actually have a blade made of glass, but
instead a metal blade, and glass was
prepared and used during the enchantment
process to make the magic sword and give
the sword it's qualities.
\LB    Many items, especially weapons,
grant skills that a character can use
when they equip the item.  Some skills
can be used only during combat, some only
outside of combat, and either one can
apply for other skills.  Almost all items
that grant skills will eventually break
after skills it grants are used enough
times, so using a special sword attack
that equipping a longsword grants will
eventually wear out the sword.  Helpful
hint: Keep spares.  In the event that
two items grant the same skill, using
that skill wears down the item that first
appears closest to the top of all of the
equipment slots for the character.  Note
that some items will last a long time,
while other items will break after their
skills are used only a few times.  (Magic
wands, for example, are notorious for
being very perishable and breaking rather
quickly.)
>

armor and defense scores stop less damage
that they do.  Axes also do the most
damage of all melee weapons. Like swords,
most axes do physical damage, and there
are also enchanted ones that do elemental
damage as well.  Axes are typically
wielded by Axemaster class characters.
>
<tjsInfo2:
    Axes don't typically require or
use any Magic Points from a character's
spirit to operate.  Basic attacks don't
cost any Tactical Points either, and do
damage based upon one's strength score
and the level of the axe.
\LB    Axes are very slow compared
to other melee weapons, and do a rather
large amount of damage by comparison.
They increase a character's maximum
Tactical Points by a decent amount when
equipped.  They add more to Tactical
Points than dual axes, and also
somewhat increase the rate at which
Tactical Points are gained and recovered.
Axes of all kinds have the highest
chances to cause a target to bleed for a
few turns when struck with a serious
blow, more so than any other melee
weapons.
\LB    Melee weapons and other types of
items have levels, and versions of an
item with a higher level are more
expensive when purchased from a merchant
but do more damage when wielded by a
character with the same starting strength
score.  Different level versions of a
weapon or other item have associated
materials that are in the name of the
item, such as "iron" or "glass" or
"marble" for example, which refer to
reagents used and consumed during the
artificing process to enchant and create
such items, which are typically magical.
As an example, a "glass sword" doesn't
actually have a blade made of glass, but
instead a metal blade, and glass was
prepared and used during the enchantment
process to make the magic sword and give
the sword it's qualities.
\LB    Many items, especially weapons,
grant skills that a character can use
when they equip the item.  Some skills
can be used only during combat, some only
outside of combat, and either one can
apply for other skills.  Almost all items
that grant skills will eventually break
after skills it grants are used enough
times, so using a special sword attack
that equipping a longsword grants will
eventually wear out the sword.  Helpful
hint: Keep spares.  In the event that
two items grant the same skill, using
that skill wears down the item that first
appears closest to the top of all of the
equipment slots for the character.  Note
that some items will last a long time,
while other items will break after their
skills are used only a few times.  (Magic
wands, for example, are notorious for
being very perishable and breaking rather
quickly.)
>

<tjsInfo:
(Magic Staff) A spellcaster's weapon,
magic staves magically fire energy bolts
of various types, and don't require any

can fire bolts that do various types of

weapons, a magic staff will eventually

replaced.  A magic staff can be held and
used with one hand, allowing the other
hand to be free for some other purpose,
although not all spellcasters can equip
and use shields, regardless of their
equipped primary weapons.

    A Hasted Magic Staff is different
from a common magic staff, enchanted when
it is made to attack twice in one combat
action instead of only once.  Both
attacks will target the same enemy, one
firing right after the other.  This can
defeat enemies faster, but has a price
tag, which is that it wears out to the
point where it breaks twice as fast as
a typical, common magic staff.  Hasted
magic staves also have a speed bonus, so
attacking with them in combat will make
the character's attack a little sooner
than when attacking with a common magic
staff, possibly before other characters
on both sides act.
>
